lines.text: Why did President Eisenhower spend hundreds of billions of dollars constructing forty-eight thousand miles of interstate highways?
It wasn't just to make cross-country road trips scenic and convenient for families.
In nineteen nineteen, a young officer named Dwight Eisenhower crossed America with a military convoy, taking sixty-two grueling days over dirt tracks.
During World War Two, he witnessed the sheer logistical speed of the German Autobahn.
In nineteen fifty-six, he signed the National Defense Highway Act to evacuate cities during nuclear attacks and move tanks nationwide in days.
Overpasses were built with sixteen-foot clearances specifically to accommodate intercontinental ballistic missile convoys.
The interstate highway system remains the largest public works project in American history.
